body:
scripts/preflight.sh runs five checks — identity, project root, repo/ checkout,
STOP files, autopilot test suite — and NONE of them consults main's build status:

    grep -nE 'gh run|gh api.*(check-runs|commits)|conclusion|statusCheckRollup' \
         scripts/preflight.sh   ->   no matches

The comment at scripts/autopilot-tick.sh:156 says "a genuinely red main still reds
preflight". That is true only of the working tree being dirty, not of CI. A red
main passes preflight cleanly today.

Consequence: the only thing between a red main and a published tag is the
judgement inside /CWNG_goal_act plus /CWNG_verify. Everything mechanical upstream
of that is blind to it, which is the wrong shape for a gate that guards an
irreversible act (a published release can never be retracted).

Note the failure mode is NOT the one you would guess. On main pushes the lanes all
run for real (Detect changed paths is skipped; Fast/Frontend/Integration/E2E ran
15/9/18/21 steps) and Test Suite Summary DID report failure when e2e failed. So the
summary is not laundering skipped lanes here. The exposure is CANCELLED runs:
concurrency cancel-in-progress cancels superseded runs, Test Suite Summary gates on
result == "failure", and "cancelled" is neither success nor failure (F-81d428). Two
recent main runs are in that state.
title: preflight never checks main's CI, so a tick can drain onto a red main
